Continue your pursuit onto Route 213 , where you find the Grunt on the narrow strip of sand midway through the route. Speak to him, and he reveals that the item in his possession was created with the energy taken from the Valley Windworks . He claims that only a scientific genius could make such an item, so the Team Galactic boss, who created it, must be a genius. The Grunt then notices your presence; though tired of running away, he still refuses to waste energy battling you.

Follow the Grunt through the grounds of Hotel Grand Lake , where you catch up to him near the stairways leading east to Route 222 . Nearly exhausted, he mentions a new universe that the boss intends to create, then hurries off to the north after realizing that he's been spotted.
By the time you catch up to him near the entrance to Lake Valor , the exhausted Grunt cannot run any longer and finally draws you into battle.

After the battle, the weary Grunt slowly makes his escape, intending to deliver the package to his Commander. Move northward to find Cynthia ; speak to her, and she asks how your Pokédex progress is going. She explains that she is here to research the folklore involving the lake, but it seems as though the lake is closed to the public right now. She goes on to tell the story of the lake, of how there is an island in the middle, how a mirage of a Pokémon is found inside, and how no one must enter that chamber. Moving on, Cynthia asks if you have seen the group of Psyduck on Route 210 . She then gives you the SecretPotion to treat their headaches, and expresses her hope that you get to meet every kind of Pokémon, and leaves to the north.

Route 212 leads northwest from Pastoria City back to Hearthome City . The path weaves around the deep puddles left by the relentless rainfall. A large estate known as the Pokémon Mansion is located just south of Hearthome, and occupies nearly half of the route.

The house on the riverbank belongs to a blonde woman, a former employee of the Weather Institute in the far-off Hoenn region. According to her sister, the woman collects Shards because they remind her of where she used to work. In exchange for 10 Shards of the same color, she offers a Technical Machine containing a weather -changing move. Each TM may be obtained repeatedly.
The Pokémon Mansion is a large residence owned by Mr. Backlot , the same man who owns Amity Square in Hearthome City . His famous Trophy Garden is located behind the building.

The Trophy Garden is Mr. Backlot 's pride and joy. As he explains, wild Pokémon are attracted to the garden, eliminating the need to travel afar to find them. It is notably the only place to find Pichu and Pikachu in the wild.

After a certain point , Mr. Backlot 's butler will begin adding certain Pokémon not normally found in Sinnoh to the garden. This is done in an attempt to cover for Backlot's claims of encountering the unfamiliar Pokémon while on a walk, which would be impossible. A different imported Pokémon appears after 24 hours have passed.

On the second visit to Hearthome City , the Gym Leader is nowhere to be found, so it seems that challenging the Hearthome Gym will need to wait a bit longer. With Cynthia 's SecretPotion in hand, use Fly , or pass through Route 209 again, to return to Solaceon Town and continue north to Route 210 .

Route 210 runs north from Solaceon Town , leading to Celestic Town far to the northwest, and Route 215 as the path turns eastward. The path passes between mountains, and was made by clearing an overgrown canyon. The northernmost areas are always covered by fog.

On the second visit to Route 210 , examine the group of Psyduck to find that they are still not inclined to move. Follow Cynthia 's advice and use the SecretPotion to cure the Pokémon of their chronic headache. Now that they're feeling better, the group wanders northward and out of sight.

Cynthia appears a moment later. Though no one knows the cause of Psyduck's chronic headaches, she is happy to see that the SecretPotion has relieved their pain. She goes on to ask a favor: deliver her Old Charm to her grandmother in Celestic Town . As there are rare Pokémon to be found on the way, she points out that it would be worth your while to accept. Do so, and she hands the Old Charm to you. Cynthia describes her grandmother as the bossy elder of Celestic Town, which happens to lie at the northwest end of the route. She then leaves to the south.

After passing through the long grass patch and reaching the end of the dirt path, you find that the northern part of the route is covered by a layer of dense fog. Though not required to continue, Defog can be used to clear the haze away and improve visibility for the road ahead.

Celestic Town is a tiny town situated between Route 210 to the east and Route 211 to the west. It is also one of the oldest, where residents preserve the region's history and the old ways of life. The center of town features a shrine that dates back to ancient times, and a cave known as the Celestic Ruins . Despite lacking a modern Poké Mart, an elderly couple runs a shop from their home in the northwest.

As you approach the southern stairway leading to the shrine, you are stopped by an elderly woman standing nearby, who warns of an odd-looking "spaceman" in front of the ruins. Learning that the cave holds nothing special only seemed to make him angry, and now he threatens to blow up the town with a bomb.  In her younger years, she and her Pokémon would have punished the Grunt, but she must now leave that to you.

Speak to the Grunt, who declares the town "insignificant" as it holds nothing he deems to be of value. He argues that since it doesn't need to exist, he'll just blow it up with a Galactic Bomb, and threatens to defeat you in battle if you interfere. He asks if you still intend to do so; select Yes and the battle begins!

After the battle, the Grunt is happy to leave and flees the town. A moment later, you are approached by the elderly woman from before, who introduces herself as the elder of Celestic Town . She thanks you for chasing the man away, and then notices the Old Charm you carry. She learns that Cynthia asked you to deliver it to her, and accepts the item from you. She explains that these charms were made here long ago in honor of the deity who was believed to have created Sinnoh , and are still discovered from time to time. Since you are here, the woman suggests taking a look around inside the ruins.

The Celestic Ruins are housed in a small cave in the center of town. A cave painting on the rear wall shows three strange beings arranged in a triangle around a shining sphere. Examine the ancient artwork, and the town elder arrives. She explains the legend behind the painting: there once existed a being so powerful that it was considered a deity. Three Pokémon opposed this being, balancing their power against its own. She goes on to reveal that she has a gift for you, an item that once belonged to her granddaughter : HM03 ( Surf ). This field move allows travel across bodies of water, but doing so requires the Badge from Hearthome Gym . The elder then exits the cave, leaving you to do the same.

Outside, you find the mysterious man from Mt. Coronet . He is aware of your recent battle here, what he calls an insignificant struggle, and suggests that everyone should view things from a bigger perspective, on a universal scale. The man introduces himself as Cyrus , and explains that he seeks the power to create a new world free of strife. He recognizes you from Mt. Coronet, and asks that you inform him if you find anything behind the legends of Sinnoh . Once he leaves, you are free to move on from the town.

The Hearthome Gym specializes in Ghost-type Pokémon. Ghost-type moves are super effective against Ghost- and Psychic-type Pokémon, while Ghost-type Pokémon are weak to Dark - and Ghost-type moves. Normal - and Fighting-type moves have no effect on Ghost-type Pokémon.

The Gym features stone construction and a multitude of wall sconces with candles burning blue to evoke the atmosphere of a haunted castle. Five stories tall, each floor features a simple mathematical puzzle posted on a sign and three doors marked with answers from which to choose. Passing through the door with the correct answer leads to an elevator to the next floor; passing through the wrong door leads to a Trainer to fight. The Gym Leader awaits all challengers on the top floor, in a room adorned with stained glass windows.

Fantina leads with her Drifblim , a Ghost / Flying Pokémon. Its high HP stat makes it difficult to take down quickly, giving it more time to use Ominous Wind . Though only a slight chance, the move may boost each of Drifblim's stats by one stage each. Her Gengar can harass its target by inducing confusion and draining its Power Points . Despite being part- Poison type, it is unafraid of Ground-type moves due to its Levitate Ability. Mismagius 's strongest move is Shadow Ball , as it may lower the target's Special Defense , giving Mismagius a chance to deal increased damage. Magical Leaf is guaranteed to hit its target; useful on its own, but especially dangerous after Shadow Ball's stat drop.
After the battle, Fantina awards you the Relic Badge , which enables the use of Surf in the field. She also gives you TM65 ( Shadow Claw ) as a prize.

Upon exiting the Gym, you are approached by Cynthia . She heard from her grandmother about the events in Celestic Town , and thanks you for what you did at the ruins. She had thought of Team Galactic as an eccentric, though harmless, bunch for their uniforms and their talk of remaking the universe, but now considers them dangerous for their plans to steal and hoard Pokémon. She then asks if you found anything interesting in the ruins, and suggests reading some of the ancient books in the Canalave City library to learn more. She then leaves to the south. Canalave City lies far to the west, beyond Jubilife City and Route 218 .
If you have not done so already, be sure to visit the Pokétch Company and speak to the president near the front desk to install the most recent app releases.
Route 218 leads west from Jubilife City to Canalave City . Despite the short distance, this path is revered by Fishermen as a great, though little known, fishing spot.

When you enter the western gate at the Canalave City limits, you are greeted by Dawn / Lucas 's father. Professor Rowan has directed him to wait here for you, with the intention of updating your Pokédex. Once this process is complete, the device will now be able to display the gender differences of a given species . He then asks if you would keep an eye on Team Galactic , as Rowan is concerned about what happened in Jubilife City . He then leaves to the east.

Located to the west of Route 218 , Canalave City is a port city that features a large canal. Formerly a hub for cargo transport, the ferry moored in this canal now transports people to and from a series of small islands off of the mainland's west coast. The Canalave Library houses many books that detail the myths of Sinnoh , and the Canalave Gym is the sixth challenge in the Sinnoh League.

The northeastern house, in front of the Pokémon Center, belongs to an elderly man known as the Move Deleter . Using his free service allows a Pokémon to forget one of its moves. This is especially useful for removing moves taught by HM , as they would normally be permanent.

The Harbor Inn is located in the northeast part of the city, behind the Pokémon Center. It was a thriving business once, until it mysteriously closed down 50 years ago. The front door has been locked tight ever since.

When you attempt to pass over the drawbridge, you are quickly approached from the west by Barry . He asks if you intend to challenge the Gym Leader , and says that someone should check that you're up to the task as he flashes his latest Gym Badge.
Afterward, Barry admits his defeat but promises to become Champion one day. He then leaves to the west.

The southwestern house belongs to a Sailor named Eldritch and his family. His wife and young son can be found inside, while he works at the nearby docks. Eldritch operates the ferry that runs between Canalave City and several small islands to the north, including Iron Island . This island may be visited at any point, though it can be a useful training ground before challenging the Canalave Gym . There are no Pokémon Centers on the remote island, so be sure to bring some healing items along. There is a gift Pokémon available there as well, so be sure to bring no more than five Pokémon in your party.

Iron Island is a small island located off the west coast of Sinnoh . It houses a cave that was once a prosperous mine, but was shut down once the reserves dried up. Since then, it has been preserved as a habitat for wild Pokémon. Members of the Canalave Gym often visit the island to train their Pokémon.
The ferry docks on the southwest part of the island. Climb up the two stairways to enter the abandoned mine.
The first chamber features two stairways leading downward. Take the stairs on the left to reach the western part of the next floor.
Move south to battle Camper Lawrence and reach the Iron Ball , then return to 1F and take the eastern stairs.

Go southward first to reach an Escape Rope . Climb onto the upper level and move eastward to reach a Super Repel near the east wall. Go down the stairway in the northeast corner, battle past Picknicker Summer, and ride the lift down to the lower level. Take the eastern stairs next.

Move eastward past Worker Willy to reach a Max Ether . Backtrack and head southward past Worker Braden to find TM23 ( Iron Tail ). Go back to the stairs in the northwest corner, then return to B1F and take the western stairs.

A short distance away from the northeast stairs, you meet a man named Riley . He has been training his Pokémon here in the abandoned mine, and warns you that the wild Pokémon here are restless. The two of you team up, and Riley promises to keep your Pokémon in perfect health. Like with Cheryl and Mira , Riley and his Lucario will assist in each battle, turning all wild battles into Double Battles , and all Trainer battles that may otherwise be Double Battles into Multi Battles .

Move westward to battle Hikers Damon and Maurice, then pick up the Ultra Ball in the northwest corner. Go south to battle Workers Brendon and Quentin, then climb the stairway to the northwest of them to find a Max Potion . Continue southward from these two Workers and pass over a series of three stairways to reach a HP Up near a group of small rocks. Move north past the two Workers and take the next tunnel headed eastward; this leads to a stairway in the southeast and a Magnet near Black Belt Kendal and Battle Girl Tyler. Move south and west to battle Ace Trainers Jonah and Brenda, then continue southward.

At the top of the lift, you and Riley encounter a pair of Galactic Grunts. Riley accuses them of causing the restlessness of the wild Pokémon, and the Grunts declare that they will take as many Pokémon as they want from the island. Riley refuses to let them get away with this, so the two of you draw the Grunts into battle.

Afterward, the Grunts quickly flee the cave, and Riley thanks you for your help. He then reveals that he has a Pokémon Egg with him, and asks if you would take it with you. Accept, and Riley says that he hopes you show the Pokémon inside all sorts of new places. He goes on to say that he will be training in other locations now, and hopes to meet you again. Ride the lift down to the lower level and step through the doorway to the west.
Ride the lift to the upper level, collect the Shiny Stone to the east, and step through the exit to the west. This leads to a shortcut back to the ferry.

The Canalave Gym specializes in Steel-type Pokémon. Steel-type moves are super effective against Ice - and Rock-type Pokémon, while Steel-type Pokémon are weak to Fighting -, Fire -, and Ground-type moves.

The Gym features four stories of disconnected steel floors, with lifts and moving platforms to carry challengers between them. On 1F, battle Black Belt Ricky to reach four yellow lifts. Take the easternmost lift near Worker Gary. On 2F, go southeast and ride the next lift down. Back on 1F, battle Ace Trainer Cesar, then ride the western lift up. Back on 2F, ride the moving platform westward to the next lift. On 3F, ride the next moving platform northward and battle Worker Gerardo. Ride eastward across two more platforms and battle Black Belt David. Move south and pass over two more platforms to reach the lift near the east wall. Back on 2F, battle past Ace Trainer Breanna and take the next lift. Back on 1F, go west and step on the red lift to reach the Gym Leader 's position.

Byron leads with his Bronzor , a Steel / Psychic Pokémon. Flash Cannon may lower the target's Special Defense , allowing Extrasensory to deal increased damage. Despite being a Steel-type Pokémon, Ground-type attacks used against it are useless due to its Levitate Ability. His Steelix makes up for its low Speed with Gyro Ball , which deals variable damage based on how much slower the user is than the target. It can also fight back with Ice Fang against Ground Pokémon that would otherwise have an advantage. Finally, his Bastiodon enjoys high physical Defense and Special Defense, and AncientPower may raise all its stats at once. Consider using status ailments like Burn or Poison to help wear it down.

After the battle, Byron awards you the Mine Badge , which enables the use of Strength in the field. Having six Badges also ensures the obedience of all Pokémon up to level 70. He also gives you TM91 ( Flash Cannon ) as a prize. Rather than backtrack through the Gym, follow the moving platforms in a clockwise direction around 3F to reach a red lift that leads directly back to 1F.
When you leave the Gym, you find Barry waiting for you. He is excited to see your new Mine Badge , and tells you to meet him at the library in the northwest part of town.

Barry can be found on the library's third floor. He greets you, then leads you to a table where Professor Rowan and Dawn / Lucas are waiting. Rowan reminds the three Trainers that he studies Pokémon Evolution, and how some Pokémon evolve while others do not. He goes on to mention the three lakes of Sinnoh , where beings that he calls mirage Pokémon are said to live. He believes that finding them may help his studies, so he directs the three of you to each investigate one of the lakes. He sends Dawn/Lucas to Lake Verity in the southwest and Barry to Lake Acuity in the north, leaving you to visit Lake Valor in the southeast.

Just then, a massive earthquake shakes the city! Rowan and the others hurry outside to find out what's happened. Rowan quickly realizes that it was not a natural occurence, while a Sailor runs past a moment later, shouting about an explosion at Lake Valor . Barry rushes off to begin his assignment while Rowan encourages you to find the cause of the explosion, noting that he and Dawn/Lucas will join you after visiting Lake Verity . Use Fly to travel southward from Veilstone City , or eastward from Pastoria City , and return to Valor Lakefront .
Unlike previous visits to Valor Lakefront , there are no longer any guards posted here. Hurry through the trees to find out what has become of Lake Valor !

It takes only a few steps from the entrance to realize that something horrible has indeed happened to Lake Valor . All of the water from the lake has been completely dried up, leaving a muddy lakebed and stranded Magikarp ! If spoken with, the first Galactic Grunt you pass seems ready to move on and do the same to Lake Verity . Follow the path southwestward, and be prepared to battle the second Galactic Grunt you pass. On the west side of the lakebed, another Grunt brags about their Galactic Bomb before drawing you into battle. Fight past a third Grunt to reach the entrance to the cavern, where another Grunt reveals that the legendary Pokémon are meant to be transported to the group's headquarters in Veilstone City .

Step inside the cavern to find one of Team Galactic 's Commanders. Speak to him, and he soon recognizes you as the Trainer who raided the Galactic Eterna Building . He says that Jupiter should be ashamed of herself for being beaten by a child, and that even the thought of opposition must not be tolerated. He then draws you into battle.

Despite his defeat, Commander Saturn promises that Team Galactic will still acquire the three legendary Pokémon of the lakes , and use their power to create a new universe. He reveals that Commander Mars should have captured the Pokémon at Lake Verity by now, and disappears in an instant. Exit the cavern and Fly back to Twinleaf Town , rest your Pokémon at home if necessary, and hurry to Lake Verity!

Professor Rowan immediately notices your arrival. He warns you that these two Galactic Grunts are after the legendary Pokémon, and that Dawn / Lucas needs your help! Defeat the two pairs of Galactic Grunts to find Rowan's assistant off to the north, where she/he is being targeted by Commander Mars . Speak to Mars, who recognizes you from the Valley Windworks . Annoyed that you seemingly do not remember her, she reintroduces herself before drawing you into battle.

After the battle, Mars shrugs off her loss, as her mission to transport the lake's Pokémon to the team's headquarters is complete. She then reveals that because of the explosion at Lake Valor , a cavern appeared here in the middle of Lake Verity . When Mesprit emerged from the cavern to help its friends, it was quickly captured. Mars brags that Team Galactic now has all three Pokémon: Mesprit, "the Being of Emotion"; Azelf , "the Being of Willpower"; and Uxie , "the Being of Intelligence". With all three, the team's plans can advance to the next phase. Mars and her subordinates disappear in an instant, leaving you, Rowan , and Dawn / Lucas to make sense of these events. Rowan is relieved that neither of you are hurt, but wonders about Barry 's wellbeing at Lake Acuity , as Uxie's capture means that his mission there has failed.

Reaching the third lake will be no easy feat, as you must first venture through Mt. Coronet and the snowbanks of Routes 216 and 217 . Be sure to prepare well for the harsh terrain ahead; after exiting the mountain, you may experience blizzard conditions, where falling hail damages all non- Ice-type Pokémon during battle. From this point, either Fly to Eterna City and go eastward, or Fly to Celestic Town and move westward, to reach the northern part of Mt. Coronet.
Route 211 is a mountain path that tunnels through the northern part of Mt. Coronet , connecting Eterna City in the west and Celestic Town in the east.

The sacred Mt. Coronet is the tallest mountain in Sinnoh , and part of a mountain range that divides the region in half. Due to its scale, an extensive tunnel system was developed in order to facilitate travel, and now connects many important cities together.

When approaching from the west entrance, begin by using Rock Smash and Strength to find TM69 ( Rock Polish ) above a ledge to the north. When approaching from the east entrance, start by collecting the Escape Rope to the south. Afterward, pick up whichever of the two items remains, then move a second boulder near the east entrance to continue northward. Use Rock Smash again to reach the Rare Candy in the dead-end tunnel to the west. Continue northward, then turn west and walk down the stairs.

The lower level is filled with mist; though not required to continue, Defog can be used to improve visibility. Use Rock Smash to collect the Stardust in the corner, then turn northward. Walk down the nearest stairway and use Surf to reach a Light Clay near the largest rock outcropping, then grab the Max Elixir on the water's northeast shore. A Revive and a Full Restore can be found on the upper level in the northeast part of the chamber. Turn west, and be sure to collect the Soft Sand on the middle level before climbing the stairs to the north.

This underground lake is the only place where wild Feebas can be found. The fish Pokémon can be very difficult to locate, as it will only appear in four separate spots and must be reeled in with a fishing rod. Unfortunately, there is no easy way to identify these four spots, as the only solution is to drop a line in each part of the lake. In addition, the location of these spots changes every day. Once found, Feebas should prove to be an easy capture. Similar to how the "pathetic" Magikarp evolves into the powerful Gyarados , the "shabby" Feebas eventually evolves into Milotic , a Pokémon famous for its beauty.
The third chamber is simply a winding tunnel. Follow the path to the exit to reach Route 216 .

Route 216 is a treacherous mountain road leading west from Mt. Coronet 's north end to Route 217 . Deep snowdrifts make it impossible to ride a bicycle here, and in some places, the snow is so deep that it cannot be run through. In addition, the constant snowfall causes hail in every battle.

A cabin known as the Snowbound Lodge can be found on the west side of the route. Inside, you find other weary travelers who have also taken refuge from the harsh weather. After hiking through Mt. Coronet and braving the winter weather, your Pokémon are likely due for a rest. Take a moment to climb into the cozy bed and examine the blankets to restore them to full health. The next city is still a good distance away, so be sure to return here to rest whenever necessary.

Route 217 runs northward from Route 216 to Acuity Lakefront . Like on the previous route, it is impossible to ride a bicycle and also difficult to run through the deep snowdrifts. Additional snowfall constantly blows down from atop Mt. Coronet , causing unending blizzard conditions that reduce visibility and cause hail to fall during every battle.

The narrow path from Route 216 opens into a large snowfield. Move north from Ace Trainer Dalton and hug the eastern side of the large group of trees. Grab the Iron a few steps to the northeast, then turn northwestward. Pick up TM07 ( Hail ) and enter to the western cabin.

Speak to the Hiker inside to learn that he dropped a Hidden Machine while pushing through the blizzard. The item can be found a short distance away to the northeast; examine it to obtain HM08 ( Rock Climb ). If spoken to again, the Hiker explains that he had already given up on finding the item, and allows you to keep it. As a reward for your honesty, he gifts you an Icicle Plate that he had found under the snow.

Leave the Hiker's cabin and move eastward to find a Max Repel nearby. Turn north-northeastward and pass by Skier Bjorn. Enter the second cabin and speak to the woman inside to receive a Spell Tag . A single icy rock can be found in the tall grass behind the cabin.

Move westward from the second cabin and follow the edge of the trees around until the path narrows again. Battle past Black Belt Luke and Ace Trainer Olivia, then pass through the second patch of tall grass to reach Acuity Lakefront .

Acuity Lakefront leads northeastward from Route 217 to Snowpoint City , and provides access to Lake Acuity to the north. The area does not experience the blizzard conditions of the previous route, giving travelers much-needed relief from the howling winds.

After traveling all the way from Canalave City to find out what happened to Barry and his investigation, you find a pair of Galactic Grunts blocking the path to Lake Acuity . If spoken with, one of them reveals that they are here standing guard so that the Snowpoint Gym Leader does not disturb the group's plans. It seems as though Barry is on his own for the moment.

Snowpoint City is located at the northern edge of the Sinnoh mainland. Harsh winds blow down from atop Mt. Coronet , bringing low temperatures and constant snowfall. The Snowpoint Gym can be found in the city's center, and a temple dedicated to a certain Legendary Pokémon stands to the north. A port on the south side allows travelers to reach the region's northeast landmass.

Like Canalave City , Snowpoint City also makes use of a ferry to allow travel to and from mainland Sinnoh . The Sailor here mentions "a great Trainer recognized by the Pokémon League", and how he looks forward to having someone like that on his ship. It seems as though riding the ferry will have to wait for the moment.

Visit the northwestern house to find a young woman who would like to trade Pokémon. She is willing to part with her Haunter in exchange for a Medicham . Haunter arrives holding an Everstone , which prevents its Evolution into Gengar .

The northeast house belongs to an elderly man. When spoken with, he asks if you would like to hear a trendy saying . Agree to learn a new word or phrase for use in the easy chat system . This can be done once per day, for a total of 32 phrases. Receiving a new trendy phrase does not alter any game mechanics .

Snowpoint Temple is a large structure on the north side of the city. A female Ace Trainer stands guard at the entrance, and explains that only the chosen few are allowed to enter. It seems that exploring the temple will need to wait until later.

The Snowpoint Gym specializes in Ice-type Pokémon. Ice-type moves are super effective against Dragon -, Flying -, Grass -, and Ground-type Pokémon, while Ice-type Pokémon are weak to Fighting -, Fire -, Rock -, and Steel-type moves.

The Gym features four floors of ice tiles, with ice-covered ramps between floors. Challengers must slide around the Gym and use their momentum to destroy snowballs blocking the path through the middle of Gym to the Gym Leader . Begin by standing two steps north of the Gym guide and slide eastward, then north to the second snowy tile. Go west to break the first snowball, climb up the stairway, then slide west and south. Climb this next stairway to reach a snowy tile, then slide north until you stop at a snowball. Slide eastward to destroy the second snowball, then go west and south to stop at another snowy tile. Slide eastward through two snowballs on the lowest level. Move south and west, climb the stairway, then move west and south again. Climb to the uppermost level, then move south and east around the corner across the three snowy tiles here. Slide north then west across the two snowy tiles in the Gym's northwest corner. Move south then east to destroy another snowball. Slide east again, then north to the Gym's northeast corner. Move to the second snowy tile to the west, then slide southward. Turn westward to destroy three more snowballs on the lowest level. Move southwest up the next two stairways again, then slide north, west, and north again. Slide eastward from here to destroy the final three snowballs on the lowest level. Slide southwest and climb up the three stairways, then move south and east to return to the entrance. From this point, slide north to reach the Gym Leader.

Candice leads with her Snover , a Grass / Ice Pokémon. As soon as it appears, its Snow Warning Ability summons a hailstorm that damages all non-Ice Pokémon. Its low physical Defense leaves it vulnerable, but beware: if damaged but not defeated in the same turn, Avalanche 's power is doubled! Her Sneasel has higher Speed and physical Attack , which pairs well with Faint Attack 's guaranteed hit and the effect of Taunt . It takes massive damage from Fighting-type moves, but Fire and Rock attacks also fare well. Medicham is a wild card; though it is not Ice type, it does have an Ice attack. Attack with Flying - and Ghost-type moves for greatest effect. Finally, her Abomasnow 's Snow Warning summons another hailstorm when it appears. Though its Speed is still relatively low, it is more offensively-oriented than Snover. Wood Hammer and Avalanche are its strongest attacks, while Swagger and GrassWhistle let it further harass its target. Hit it with Fire moves for best results, but Fighting and Rock moves, among others, are also effective.
After the battle, Candice awards you the Icicle Badge , which enables the use of Rock Climb in the field. She also gives you TM72 ( Avalanche ) as a prize.
On the second visit to Acuity Lakefront , the two Galactic Grunts have moved aside and no longer block the path to Lake Acuity . Hurry ahead to find out what has become of Barry !

Lake Acuity is the third of the three lakes of Sinnoh . After the explosion at Lake Valor , a cave appeared here in the middle of the lake. This cave is said to be home Uxie , the "Being of Intelligence".

When you reach Lake Acuity , you find Barry having just lost to Jupiter . She taunts him, asking if he really thought he could be the one to save the Pokémon of the lake. This is short-lived, however, as she dislikes the cold weather and is anxious to return to the Galactic HQ . She recognizes you as she turns to leave, and states that Team Galactic intends to do something huge for everyone's sake. She warns you to stay out of the group's way, and to stay away from their headquarters in Veilstone City .
After Jupiter leaves, you automatically move to check on Barry . He is distraught over his defeat and having witnessed Uxie 's suffering. He promises to get tougher, and exits the area.

A single Galactic Grunt can be found outside the Galactic HQ building on the northeast hill. If spoken with, he reveals that because of you, his superiors took away his Clefairy and his partner quit the team to return to his home country. He suspiciously claims to know nothing about any Storage Key and rushes off before you can question him about it. In his haste, he drops an item in front of you, which turns out to be a Storage Key .

The Storage Key doesn't seem to work on the electronic door on the Galactic HQ 's first floor, but it must belong somewhere. Leave the building and hurry westward to try the Galactic Warehouse instead.

Examine the rust-covered door to unlock it with the Storage Key , which then snaps off inside the keyhole. Pick up the Dusk Stone beyond the door and take the stairs down to the lower part of the basement.

At the bottom of the stairs, the path diverges. The northbound hallway leads to a locked door, so instead move eastward and battle a Galactic Grunt. Continue past him and pick up a Zinc in the storage room. Battle a second Grunt to continue and climb the eastern stairs.

There is a single Grunt on B1F. He has no Pokémon, however, and blames it on the fact that he still doesn't know how the building's warp panels connect. Continue past him and climb the eastern stairs to the Galactic HQ building's ground floor.

The underground hallway leads to the northeast room on the first floor. Defeat the female Grunt and turn the corner to reach a pair of warp panels . Step on the warp to the right first; this leads to the eastern part of the southeast room. Pick up TM49 ( Snatch ) and warp back to the northeast room. Take the warp on the left this time to continue.
Move south and step on the next warp panel to reach the next room.
Climb up the stairs to reach the second floor.
Ignore the Grunt and the stairs to the east for now, and step on the warp panel to the west instead.
Head eastward and take the stairs back down to 1F.
Move westward past Scientist Fredrick and take the stairs down to the basement level.

Go west and pass by the Galactic Grunt to reach TM36 ( Sludge Bomb ) in a puddle to the south. Continue westward to find a Galactic Key . With this key card, you can unlock the electronic doors to the west to create a shortcut to the warehouse entrance.
It's time to storm Team Galactic's headquarters ! Leave the warehouse and enter the HQ building through the western or central doors.
Examine the electronic doors to unlock them with the Galactic Key . Climb up the stairs to 2F.
Go east and battle the two Grunts in a potential Multi Battle . Continue on to reach the Team Galactic TV Room, where Scientist Darrius can be battled.

There are two warp panels to the east of the TV Room. The northern warp leads to 2F (West), a small storage room with cardboard boxes. The southern warp leads to 2F (Southwest), where another warp leads to 2F (Southeast) and a Max Revive . Afterward, return to the TV Room and step on the warp here.

Furnished with a pair of comfy beds, the second floor's northeast room seems to be a breakroom. Take advantage of the opportunity and rest your Pokémon if necessary, then climb up the nearby stairs to continue.

Go west to fight two more Grunts in another Multi Battle . Continue westward to find three warp panels . Both the eastern and central warps lead to 3F (Southeast); the eastern warp leads to a dead-end while the central one leads to an Elixir . Afterward, backtrack and take the western warp.
Move east and climb up the stairs to 4F.

Go east and use the Galactic Key to unlock the door and approach the Team Galactic boss. Cyrus realizes that you must be the Trainer trying to stand up to Team Galactic. He has heard of the trouble that you have caused for his Commanders, and knows that you're here to save Uxie , Mesprit , and Azelf . He claims to no longer have any need for them, and does not care to stop you as he says it would save him the trouble of disposing of them. Cyrus is fascinated by you, as you have no connection to the lake guardians but are here to rescue them anyway. He reaffirms his belief that emotions like pity and compassion are "useless", "illogical", and "irrational", and are merely products of the weak human heart. He intends to make you regret listening to these emotions, and draws you into battle.

Defeated, Cyrus admits that your power lies in your compassion toward Pokémon. He calls such emotions a waste, mere illusions that fade over time. This is the reason he gives for abandoning all emotion as "useless sentimentality". He recognizes that you will never understand his position, and that you are strong and courageous to come here alone. Since he does not view Pokémon as friends like Trainers do, or even as tools like Team Galactic does, he rewards you with an item that he has no need for: a Master Ball , the highest grade of Poké Ball and one that is guaranteed to catch its target.

To save the Pokémon from the lakes, Cyrus invites you to take the warp panel in the room ahead. He reveals that he will be heading to the peak of Mt. Coronet , where he will bring about "a new beginning for everything". He then leaves to the east. Follow his lead and take the warp in the eastern room to reach another part of 4F.

The second part of the fourth floor consists of a single, dimly-lit hallway lined by large machines filled with green fluid. Neither of the two Scientists here are interested in battling, and instead express regret for their involvement in the team's actions. Proceed down the hallway and pass through the door at the end.

Inside the final room, you immediately find Uxie imprisoned within some type of machine; it appears to be suffering, with its eyes tightly shut. Mesprit and Azelf are confined within other machines and seem to be suffering as well. Saturn can be seen standing at the large machine in the center of the room. Speak to him, and he wonders why Cyrus would let a child like you come and go freely. He then draws you into battle in order to get payback for his defeat at Lake Valor .

Defeated, Saturn tells you to do whatever you want with the three lake guardians , and instructs you to push the red button on the large machine to set them free. Do so, and the three Pokémon escape their confinement and disappear in an instant. Saturn explains that Cyrus crafted a Red Chain from crystals that he took from the three Pokémon; this chain is apparently meant to restrain something on Mt. Coronet . Saturn says that this is all he knows, and disappears in an instant, as well. Backtrack through the hallway and take the warp back to Cyrus' office. Once there, go south and take the green warp panel for a shortcut to the exit.
The path to the peak of Mt. Coronet is a grueling one, so be sure to prepare well.
When ready, Fly to Oreburgh City and go northeast, or Hearthome City and go west, to return to Mt. Coronet.
On this latest visit to Mt. Coronet , Cyrus is about to put his endgame into motion. Chase him to the mountaintop to put a stop to Team Galactic 's plans once and for all!
Surf eastward across the northern pool of water. Use Rock Climb to scale the wall and climb up the stairs in the northeast corner.

Go northwest and collect the Max Potion from the hill to the north. Turn the corner to the west and proceed to the southern wall to reach an Escape Rope . Head north and climb up the nearest stairway to find two diverging paths, one leading west and one leading north.

Take the western path first, and pass through the exit to reach the uppermost level of Route 207 . Use Rock Climb to reach the cliff below and collect the Iron . Climb back up the cliffside and re-enter the cave.

Go north from the stairway and cross over the western bridge. Walk down the next stairway, then detour to the south to reach TM80 ( Rock Slide ). Turn north and pass under the bridge this time, then collect the Revive to the northwest. Cross over the larger eastern bridge, then double-back and pass underneath it to reach the doorway in the northwest.
Go northeast and climb up the stairs.
Move north and battle the first Galactic Grunt. Follow the tunnel southwestward to battle a second Grunt and pass through the next doorway.
The upper part of the mountain stands high in the sky, and is constantly covered in snow. All battles that take place here will be affected by hail .
Go northeast and use Rock Climb to scale the next cliff. Turn west and pass through the large grass patch, or use Strength to move the boulder and bypass it, and enter the western doorway.

Head north and use Rock Climb to scale the cliff. Continue northward and battle the next Grunt. Turn east and battle the second Grunt here. Walk down the stairway and go east to return to the mountainside.
Head to the northeast and walk down the stairway. Go north and enter the nearby doorway.

Defeat the nearby Grunt, then use Rock Climb to descend. Follow the eastern wall northward and fight the next two Grunts. Go west, then south and walk down the two stairways. Head south and use Rock Climb. The Grunt to the north is hopelessly lost, and blocks a shortcut to the tunnel linking Eterna City and Celestic Town . Go south and use Rock Smash to pass through the rocky debris. Use Rock Climb once in the southwest, then again to return to the mountainside.

Move north and use Rock Climb to scale the cliff to the west. Continue westward through the tall grass, or use Strength to move the boulder and bypass it. Step through the cave entrance in the northwest.
This part of the mountain is only a tunnel. Climb up the stairs to the east to proceed.
Turn south and climb up the first stairway to battle another Grunt. Climb the second stairway to battle a second Grunt on the upper level, then climb the western stairs.
Turn north and battle one last Grunt on the middle level, then take the exit to reach the mountaintop.

The Spear Pillar is the name of the archaeological site on the highest peak of Mt. Coronet . These broken marble columns are the ruins of an ancient temple destroyed centuries ago when the masters of time and space last entered our world. Cyrus cannot be allowed to summon the Legendary Pokémon!
When you try to climb up onto the marble platform, you are stopped by a pair of Grunts and drawn into a Multi Battle .

Press onward, and you will soon find Jupiter , Mars , and Cyrus , making their final preparations in order to remake the world. When you approach, Cyrus declares that it is time for all to end and everything to begin. He plans to use the Red Chain to pry open a portal to another dimension, and use the power of Dialga, the master of time D / Palkia, the master of space P , for himself! A glowing portal appears to the north, and the Legendary Pokémon emerges. As its power begins to affect all of Sinnoh , Cyrus declares that this is how he will bring on the destruction of all things, in order to eliminate all fighting and strife. He believes that the current world cannot be molded into the one he desires, and that it is far easier to create a new one instead, a world where he rules over all!

Move northward to confront Jupiter and Mars . They know that you're in a hurry to stop Cyrus , but each has their own score to settle with you. Just as it seems that they will gang up on you with a two-on-one battle, Barry appears and rushes to your aid! He and his six Pokémon join you in a Multi Battle against the two Commanders.

Despite having just defeated two of his Commanders, Jupiter says that you are still no match for Cyrus . Barry tells you that his Pokémon are unable to continue, and heals your Pokémon to full health for your battle with Cyrus. He wishes you well, then leaves the ruins.

Just then, the daylight dims and a spinning field of stars appears beneath the Legendary Pokémon. Cyrus is pleased to see his new universe in the making, until something goes wrong. Uxie , Mesprit , and Azelf suddenly appear and surround the Legendary Pokémon. Their powers have negated the effects of the Red Chain , breaking Cyrus' control and thwarting his plan. With the threat eliminated, the lake guardians disappear as soon as they arrive, but Mesprit pauses in front of you for a moment before following the others. Cyrus cannot understand why the Red Chain failed, or why Mesprit appeared before you. He promises to capture the lake guardians again, but intends to crush you first!

Though the battle is over, Cyrus refuses to give up and still vows to become a deity one day. But with their endgame thwarted, Cyrus, Jupiter , Mars , and the rest of Team Galactic flee the area in an instant and go into hiding as they work to regroup.

Professor Rowan and Dawn / Lucas arrive a moment later. The professor marvels at the Legendary Pokémon standing before you all, and cannot be sure if it is enraged or saddened. He says that it appears to be waiting for you, and encourages you to face it. Rowan explains that the Pokémon is out of control after being forced by the Red Chain to use its power, but seems to be entrusting you to stop it. Dawn/Lucas mentions that she/he ran into Barry a short time ago, and how he said that he is sure that you can get the job done. She/He feels the same way, and pleads with you to relieve the Pokémon of its suffering.
If run from, the Legendary Pokémon respawns upon leaving the area. If defeated, it respawns upon entering the Hall of Fame .

Dialga , the master of time, is a Steel / Dragon Pokémon. Metal Claw deals damage and may raise its physical Attack , allowing it and Dragon Claw to hit even harder. AncientPower has the potential to raise every one of its stats. Roar of Time is Dialga's signature move ; immensely powerful, but forces the user to recharge on the next turn. Use the Master Ball if you wish; otherwise, prepare for a lengthy battle. Begin with Fighting - and Ground-type attacks to wear its health down quickly before moving to weaker moves to chip away at it even further. Due to Dialga's part-Steel typing, it is immune to Poison-type moves and has many resistances, so consider lulling it to sleep or inflicting paralysis to restrict its movements. When its HP is nearly depleted, attempt capture with Dusk Balls Night or Ultra Balls for best results.

Palkia , the master of space, is a Water / Dragon Pokémon. Water Pulse deals damage and may confuse the target. AncientPower has the potential to raise every one of its stats. Spacial Rend is Palkia's signature move , a powerful attack with an increased critical hit ratio.  Use the Master Ball if you wish; otherwise, prepare for a lengthy battle. Begin with Dragon-type attacks to wear its health down quickly before moving to weaker moves to chip away at it even further. Consider lulling it to sleep or inflicting paralysis to restrict its movements. When its HP is nearly depleted, attempt capture with Dusk Balls Night , Net Balls , or Ultra Balls for best results.

When the battle is over, Professor Rowan and Dawn / Lucas arrive. Rowan is amazed at your success, saying that in his sixty years he has never been this thrilled. Dawn/Lucas informs you that the professor has done a lot of research since your last meeting and became very concerned about you, leading him to visit this treacherous place. She/He is glad to see you safe, and leads you toward the exit. Alone in the ruins, Rowan declares that no one has the right to take away anyone else's future or anyone else's world.

Afterward, you find yourself standing with Professor Rowan and Dawn / Lucas near the exit from Mt. Coronet . Before leaving, however, be sure to visit the north side of the ruins and collect the legendary artifact there. When held by Dialga , the Adamant Orb D boosts the power of its Steel - and Dragon-type attacks by 20%. When held by Palkia , the Lustrous Orb P boosts the power of its Water - and Dragon-type attacks by 20%.

When you are ready to leave, venture back inside Mt. Coronet . Using an Escape Rope now will immediately return you to the foot of the mountain. Otherwise, you will need to backtrack through 6F, 5F, and 4F (3) again. On the Mountainside, enter the cave opening near the northeast stairway, then take the Tunnel's north exit. Back in 1F (North), pick up TM02 ( Dragon Claw ) nearby as you follow the narrow tunnel northward. Use Strength to move the boulder, then exit through the east to Celestic Town .

With the events at Spear Pillar concluded, data for Dialga D / Palkia P has now been recorded in your Pokédex . However, it is impossible to encounter the opposite Pokémon, leaving a missing page in the device. To rectify this, return to Celestic Town and visit the large home on the north side. Speak to Cynthia 's grandmother to learn that she has done more research since the incident at the local ruins. She has discovered an old book in the shrine, and points out a page that displays an image of Palkia P /Dialga D . Viewing this image is critical for completing the Pokédex.
Route 222 leads east from Valor Lakefront to Sunyshore City . The sandy beach is always busy with avid Fishermen happily casting their lines at the water's edge.

Sunyshore City was founded on a narrow stretch of rocky coastline, surrounded by the sea and mountains. Solar panels were eventually installed, serving as both power generation and a means of travel for the city to expand to the surrounding islands. The Vista Lighthouse stands tall on the southeast island, and the Sunyshore Gym , eighth in the Sinnoh League, is located in the northwest.

Upon exiting the gate from Route 222 , you are approached by a man with red hair. He instantly recognizes the toughness of your Pokémon, and introduces himself as Flint , one of the Pokémon League 's Elite Four . He goes on to explain an idea of his that involves the local Gym Leader. There have apparently been few good challengers lately, and as a result, the Gym Leader has lost his enthusiasm for the job and spends his days renovating the Gym, which led to the recent citywide blackout. Flint asks that you give the man a battle so hot that it will lift his mood and reignite his passion for battling. He then leaves to the east.

The Sunyshore Market is located on the west side of the city, just north of the Poké Mart. The market is famous for its wide selection of Seals from around the world. These Seals can be purchased from the man at the northwest table, with availability changing based on the day of the week.
In addition, the woman at the stall near the entrance awards an Effort Ribbon to your lead Pokémon, if it has earned 510 effort values .

There are two homes on the northeast island, the eastern of which belongs to a woman named Julia . Her husband is a Sailor and often spends long periods of time away from home. To help pass the time until his return, she asks that you visit occasionally and tell her stories of your travels. If you return starting tomorrow to relive tales of your adventures, she will reward you with one of seven Ribbons to be attached to your lead Pokémon. The type of Ribbon earned depends on the day of the week.

When you arrive at the Sunyshore Gym to challenge the Gym Leader , you find Flint standing outside. He informs you that the man has not yet returned, and reminds you to give him an intense battle when he does so.

The Vista Lighthouse is located on the southeast side of the city. Step inside to reach the elevator, which automatically rises to the observation deck. A blond man can be seen peering through a pair of binoculars. Speak to him, and he recognizes you as the Sunyshore Gym 's latest challenger. The man declares that if he finds you weak, he intends to challenge the Pokémon League . As the renovations to the Gym are complete, he would rather go searching for battles that thrill him again. He vows that as the strongest Gym Leader in Sinnoh , he will unleash everything he has to defeat you. He then leaves through the elevator.
If examined, the binoculars show the Pokémon League building, located far to the north above a waterfall.

Make your way to the Gym and speak to Flint outside. He informs you that the Gym Leader has returned and seemed to be feeling upbeat for a change. Flint believes that the man recognized your toughness right away, and likely can't wait to battle you. He reminds you again to give the Gym Leader a battle intense enough to reignite his love of battling. He mentions that he will be waiting at the Pokémon League , then leaves to the east.

The Sunyshore Gym specializes in Electric-type Pokémon. Electric-type moves are super effective against Flying - and Water-type Pokémon, while Electric-type Pokémon are weak to Ground-type moves. As the Gym also features several non-Electric Pokémon, Dark -, Grass -, and Fighting-type moves will also be useful.

The Gym features large gears and exposed electricity. Challengers must step on buttons in the floor to rotate these gears and create a path forward. Blue buttons rotate their gears by 90 degrees clockwise, green buttons rotate their gears 90 degrees counterclockwise, and red gears rotate by 180 degrees. In the first room, there are two green buttons. Step on the eastern button first, then the western one, and battle School Kid Tiera. In the second room, step on the southern blue button three times, then walk up the southwest stairway and cross over the gear there. Battle School Kid Forrest in the northeast corner, then step on the northern blue button once. Step on the green button next, then battle Guitarist Jerry. Climb the eastern stairway and battle Poké Kid Meghan to reach the third room. Once there, step on the eastern red button first, then the western one. Battle Ace Trainer Destiny, then walk along the west wall to battle Guitarist Preston in the northwest corner. Step on the green northwest button twice, then the blue button to the east. Walk down the stairway to battle Ace Trainer Zachery, then pass by Guitarist Lonnie again. Step on the eastern red button, then backtrack along the east wall to reach the Gym Leader .

Volkner leads with his Raichu , an Electric-type Pokémon. Charge Beam deals damage and is likely to raise its Special Attack , letting the move hit harder the next time. Light Screen halves the damage done by special moves , but avoid using just any physical move instead, as its Static Ability may paralyze the foe on contact . Though not an Electric-type Pokémon, his Ambipom can be just as dangerous. Nasty Plot and Agility raises its Special Attack and Speed , respectively, and Baton Pass lets it pass these changes to its next teammate. Shock Wave never misses its target, and receives a power boost from its Technician Ability. Octillery , a Water-type Pokémon, lets Volkner fight back against Ground-type Pokémon that might otherwise have the advantage. Both Octazooka and Aurora Beam benefit from Charge Beam's possible power boost, while they and Bullet Seed all deal serious damage to Ground Pokémon. Volkner's final Pokémon, Luxray , has high physical Attack . Crunch may lower the target's physical Defense , allowing it and Thunder Fang to hit harder than normal. Be aware of its Rivalry Ability, which lets it deal increased damage to other male Pokémon and decreased damage to female Pokémon.

After the battle, Volkner exclaims that this was the most fun he's had in a battle in ages. He awards you the Beacon Badge , which enables the use of Waterfall in the field. Having all eight Badges also ensures the obedience of all Pokémon, regardless of level. He also gives you TM57 ( Charge Beam ) as a prize.

With the Sunyshore Gym defeated, take a moment to rest at the Pokémon Center before heading north. Speak to the woman on the beach, and she mentions how the city makes her feel at home somehow, as it is next to the sea and features a lighthouse. Noticing your new Beacon Badge , she realizes that you must be a strong Trainer. To reward your training, she gives you HM07 ( Waterfall ), a field move that is essential for reaching the Pokémon League to the north.

Route 223 leads north from Sunyshore City to the island that holds the Pokémon League . This stretch of ocean is littered with rocks and sandbars, forcing travelers to navigate around these obstacles to proceed. It is a favorite training spot for Swimmers.

The island that holds the Pokémon League is located to the north of Sunyshore City , jutting up far above the ocean. A large waterfall ensures that only the strongest Trainers reach it. In order to reach the castle on the north side where the Elite Four and Champion await, determined challengers must first find their way through Victory Road .

Victory Road is a sprawling cave network that separates the south side of the Pokémon League island from the north side. It is the last and toughest of the trials leading up to the Pokémon League challenge. Surf , Strength , Rock Smash , Waterfall , and Rock Climb are all required to reach the other side.

Cross northward over the bridge, then use Rock Climb to reach the lower level. Go west to battle Psychic Bryce and collect TM41 ( Torment ) to the north. Use Rock Climb again to return to the upper level, then go east over the second bridge. Walk down the stairway and head north to battle Bird Keeper Hana and pick up the Full Heal . Climb back up the stairway, go north over the third bridge, and use Rock Climb to climb down. Go west and pass between the two ledges and walk up the stairway. Move northward to battle Ace Trainer Mariah, then climb the nearby stairway to reach the second floor.

Go west and use Rock Smash to clear the debris, then use Strength . Move the first boulder westward, then the second boulder eastward. Get out the Bicycle and press the B Button to shift to fourth gear, then jump the ramp. Use Rock Smash to clear the way, then shift to third gear and jump the second ramp. Go north to reach a Max Ether , then jump the ledge. Shift back to fourth gear, jump over the ramp, then jump down the ledge to return to the stairs from 1F.

Turn southward and clear the way with Rock Smash . Farther south, you find a group of three boulders. Use Strength and move the eastern one south, then the western one west, and then the southwest one southward. Go west and battle Ace Trainer Omar. Push the western of the two nearby boulders southward, clear the broken rock to the south, then move it back to its original position. Clear another broken rock to battle Ace Trainer Sydney. To the east, another group of three boulders can be found. Move the northern boulder eastward; this allows for northward travel but blocks the eastern tunnel. Go north to battle Veteran Clayton and walk down the stairs.
Move eastward over the bridge, then use Rock Climb to reach the lower level. Go northeast to battle Black Belt Miles, then walk down the stairs to the east.

Walk down the next two stairways and Surf across the first pool of water to battle Psychic Valencia. Surf out around her, then cross the pool to the southeast. Battle Double Team Jo & Pat, then cross the southernmost pool and climb the stairs to the west.
Pick up the Rare Candy , then walk back down to B1F.

Cross the southernmost pool, then go down the two stairways. Cross the second pool next to find a branching path: either Surf northward across the largest pool, or take the eastern path and battle Ace Trainer Henry. Afterward, use Waterfall to climb the wall of water and sail westward. Descend the western waterfall to reach TM59 ( Dragon Pulse ), then climb back up the water. Battle Dragon Tamer Ondrej, then turn southward and climb up the stairs.

Go as far west as possible, then turn southward to reach a Razor Claw . Backtrack a bit and climb up the stairway next to Veteran Edgar. Cross the bridge to find a Zinc , and a man blocking a cave opening. It seems as though you are not yet tough enough to pass this way, so return to Veteran Edgar and go south. The path diverges here, so take the western path first. Scale the wall with Rock Climb , then cross the western bridge and climb the stairs beyond.
Use Strength to move both the north and south boulders westward, then the remaining boulder to either side. Collect TM79 ( Dark Pulse ) and return to 1F.
Return to the previous intersection and go east this time. Use Rock Climb to continue northward and battle Dragon Tamer Clinton. Cross the bridge to the north to reach the exit.
With Victory Road behind you, the final hurdle standing between you and the Pokémon League has fallen away. Climb the crashing wall of water with Waterfall and enter the imposing castle at the top.

The Pokémon League building holds the traditional amenities, with a Pokémon Center and PC to the left, and a Poké Mart to the right. It's a good idea to stock up on items that restore health and status ailments for the gauntlet ahead.

To proceed, you must speak to the Ace Trainer guarding the door. However, as soon as you get close enough, Barry comes rushing in. He is here to challenge the Pokémon League as well, and suggests a battle to determine the more worthy challenger.

Defeated, Barry says that he must not be ready for the Pokémon League yet. He vows to get tougher and become the Champion , and tells you not to lose to anyone before him. He then exits the building, leaving you free to continue onward.

The Pokémon League building holds the traditional amenities, with a Pokémon Center and PC to the left, and a Poké Mart to the right. It's a good idea to stock up on items that restore health and status ailments for the gauntlet ahead.

When preparations are complete, speak to the Ace Trainer guarding the doorway in the room's center. He verifies that you've earned all eight Sinnoh League Badges before stepping aside, allowing you to enter the depths of the Pokémon League. Challengers must face the Elite Four and Champion in quick succession, with no outside help.

The first member of the Elite Four is Aaron , a master of Bug-type Pokémon. Bug-type moves are super effective against Dark -, Grass -, and Psychic-type Pokémon, while Bug-type Pokémon are weak to Fire -, Flying -, and Rock-type moves.

Aaron leads with his Dustox , a Bug / Poison Pokémon. Double Team and Light Screen make it harder to hit while Toxic steadily drains the target's health. While Dustox acts more defensively, Beautifly is more offense-oriented. Each of its moves may lower the target's Special Defense ; this pairs well with its higher Special Attack to keep up the pressure. His Vespiquen 's Attack Order rallies its underlings to fight, and Defend Order boosts its already-high defenses. Power Gem lets it fight back against predators, so Fire - and Flying-type Pokémon, beware! Heracross has the highest physical Attack of his team, and has plenty of high-powered moves to provide coverage. Stone Edge inflicts serious damage to Fire- and Flying-type Pokémon, while Close Combat crushes Rock Pokémon. Aaron's ace Pokémon is Drapion , his only non-Bug Pokémon. As a Poison / Dark Pokémon, it is only vulnerable to Ground-type attacks. Avoid facing it with Ground-type Pokémon, however, or watch out for Ice Fang !

The second member of the Elite Four is Bertha , a master of Ground-type Pokémon. Ground-type moves are super effective against Electric -, Fire -, Poison -, Rock -, and Steel-type Pokémon, while Ground-type Pokémon are weak to Grass -, Ice -, and Water-type moves.

Bertha leads with her Quagsire , a Water / Ground Pokémon. Protect and Double Team make it harder to hit, but the bigger problem is Sandstorm . This triggers a sandstorm that damages all Pokémon except Rock , Ground , and Steel types, and boosts the Special Defense of Rock Pokémon. Sudowoodo , a Rock-type Pokémon, hits hard with Earthquake and Hammer Arm . Despite its lower Special Defense, its Sturdy Ability prevents a one-hit knockout. Her Golem functions similarly to Sudowoodo, with both Earthquake and a strong Fighting-type attack. Its low Speed pairs well with Gyro Ball , dealing more damage to faster targets. Whiscash 's Water - and Psychic-type attacks provide additional coverage, but like Quagsire, it is especially vulnerable to Grass moves. Her ace Pokémon is Hippowdon , which triggers a sandstorm on its arrival with its Sand Stream Ability. Curse boosts its own power while Crunch weakens the target's physical Defense , building on the power of Earthquake and Stone Edge to make Bertha's final Pokémon a serious threat. Don't hesitate to use super effective attacks before it can score a knockout!

The third member of the Elite Four is Flint , a master of Fire-type Pokémon. Fire-type moves are super effective against Bug -, Grass -, Ice -, and Steel-type Pokémon, while Fire-type Pokémon are weak to Ground -, Rock -, and Water-type moves.

Flint leads with his Rapidash . Sunny Day intensifies the sun's rays , boosting the power of all Fire moves and weakening all Water moves. In addition, SolarBeam may be used without charging first, letting Flint fight back against Ground -, Rock -, and Water-type Pokémon. His Steelix , a Steel / Ground Pokémon, can lower the target's physical Defense with Screech . Its own physical Defense is nearly impenetrable, so attack with special moves instead. Drifblim , a Ghost / Flying Pokémon, tends to use Will-O-Wisp to burn the foe. Ominous Wind may boost every stat by one stage, a benefit that can then be passed to a teammate with Baton Pass . Use moves that do not make contact to avoid triggering its Aftermath Ability. His Lopunny 's Cute Charm Ability may infatuate female attackers when hit with a contact move. Like Steelix, it takes serious damage from Fighting-type attacks. Flint's ace Pokémon is Infernape , only the second Fire Pokémon on his team. Flare Blitz and Earthquake hit hard while Mach Punch lets it strike first. It is vulnerable to both Water- and Flying-type attacks, but ThunderPunch lets it retaliate against such Pokémon, so plan accordingly.

The final member of the Elite Four is Lucian , a master of Psychic-type Pokémon. Psychic-type moves are super effective against Fighting - and Poison-type Pokémon, while Psychic-type Pokémon are weak to Bug -, Dark -, and Ghost-type moves.

Lucian leads with his Mr. Mime . Reflect and Light Screen bolsters the team's defenses, so attack with physical moves or special moves depending on which may be in effect. Girafarig 's Shadow Ball lets it counter Ghost-type Pokémon. A Normal-type Pokémon, it is immune to Ghost attacks, so use Bug - or Dark-type moves against it instead. His Medicham is the team's only physical attacker. Drain Punch steals the target's health for itself, and lets it fight back against Dark-type Pokémon. Beware the power boost from its Pure Power Ability. Three of Alakazam 's moves build on its high Special Attack by lowering the target's Special Defense . Use powerful physical moves to target Alakazam's low physical Defense . Lucian's ace Pokémon is Bronzong , a Steel / Psychic Pokémon with high defenses. Calm Mind boosts the damage output from Psychic, and Gyro Ball deals more damage against faster opponents. Its Levitate Ability protects it from Ground-type moves, so attack with physical Fire -, Ghost -, or Dark-type moves instead.

With the Elite Four defeated, you have earned the right to challenge the reigning Champion of the Sinnoh region. Be sure to make any preparations before entering the final room, as you will be drawn into battle almost immediately.

Inside the Champion's hall, you find Cynthia waiting for you. She asks how you have been, and thanks you for your help at Mt. Coronet . She can sense the power you learned from overcoming all previous challenges, and is excited to see it in battle. The stage is set for a legendary showdown! Her Pokémon are of many different types, and don't share one common weakness as the Elite Four's teams do. However, Grass -, Fire -, and Ice-type attacks will be the most useful. With such a varied team, be sure to switch out your Pokémon as needed to capitalize on her Pokémon's weaknesses. Use your best strategies and your strongest attacks to bring down the Champion!
With the battle concluded, Cynthia congratulates you on your impressive victory. She is glad to take part in the crowning of Sinnoh 's new Champion, and instructs you to take the lift.

She catches up to you in the next room, a room lined with Pokémon statues and green lights in the floor. She explains that the room ahead is the Hall of Fame , but is interrupted by the arrival of Professor Rowan . Rowan compliments your latest battle, and says how it is only natural that he would come to witness the crowning achievement of a Trainer he enlisted in his Pokédex project. Cynthia then asks you to follow her, and for Rowan to join the two of you.

Cynthia leads both you and Professor Rowan into the Hall of Fame room, where all victorious Pokémon and thier Champions are honored. Once you set your Pokémon on the machine here, the details of both you and your party members are recorded. During the process, a shot of each Pokémon appears briefly on-screen. The screen fades to black, the game is saved, and the credits begin to roll.

When the game resumes, you find yourself back home in Twinleaf Town . Walk downstairs to find your mother , who informs you that Barry was here looking for you a short time ago. He was apparently shouting about you needing to board a ship in Snowpoint City , but rushed off before she could get any more information.

When you return to Sandgem Town , you find Dawn / Lucas standing outside Professor Rowan 's lab. If spoken with, she/he asks to take a look at your Pokédex, and if you have shown it to the professor yet.

Visit the Pokémon Research Lab to meet with Professor Rowan . The Sinnoh regional Pokédex is evaluated based on the number of different Pokémon species seen, and is considered complete once it includes 150 entries. If you have battled every Trainer and encountered every available Pokémon species in each area, your Pokédex should be at or near completion. If complete, Rowan is thrilled to see that you have recorded data on every Pokémon in Sinnoh , and excited for how much this will help with his research.

An elderly man soon enters and greets Rowan, and mentions what a long trip it was from the Kanto region. Rowan introduces the man as Professor Oak , the world's authority on Pokémon. He then introduces you to Oak, and explains that you filled out every page of the Sinnoh Pokédex for him. Oak is impressed with what he has heard about you, and mentions that he is here on an errand for Rowan. The professor has asked Oak to bring the data needed to update the Pokédex to National Mode , and Oak takes the opportunity to update your device. With 493 different species currently identified, Oak warns that completing the National Pokédex won't be easy. He goes on to mention that Pal Park is now open at the end of Route 221 , and has a system in place that attracts Pokémon from every region. He intends to visit this facility to ensure that it is operating properly, and suggests that you visit the park, as well.

After Professor Oak leaves, speak to Rowan again to receive the Poké Radar . This device is used to seek out wild Pokémon hiding in tall grass. These species are likely foreign to the Sinnoh region. The device is most notably used to increase the odds of encountering differently-colored Pokémon . Like the Vs. Seeker , its battery must be recharged after each use by walking around, and takes 50 steps to do so.

With the National Pokédex update in hand, dozens of species will begin appearing in mass outbreaks . A swarm of Pokémon will appear each day in a certain location, increasing the encounter rate for that species from 0% to 40%. Many of these Pokémon are not normally found in Sinnoh . These outbreaks only last for one day, and are determined randomly. Information on these outbreaks can be obtained by watching the special report on any TV, or by speaking to Dawn / Lucas 's sister in Sandgem Town .

With the National Pokédex update in hand, several new species may now appear in the wild. When the title screen loads while one of the Generation III games is present in the Nintendo DS 's second slot, this causes several species native to that game to appear in certain locations. Most of the Pokémon found this way are not included in the Sinnoh Pokédex , and are version-exclusive Pokémon . Each one has an 8% encounter rate, or 4% if there are two different Pokémon found this way in the same location with the same game.
Route 219 is a short route leading south from Sandgem Town to Route 220 . A pleasant breeze blows in from the sea over the beautiful white sand beach just outside of town.
Route 220 leads from Route 219 in the north to Route 221 in the east. With gentle winds and tides, the sea here is perfect for swimming.

Located on the southwest side of the Sinnoh mainland, Route 221 simply leads east from Route 220 . A straight path hemmed in by green grass and rows of trees, the gateway to Pal Park stands at its end.

Visit the house on the north side of the route and speak to the elderly man inside. He tells you a certain number, and ask to see a Pokémon of the same level. Fulfill his request, and he rewards you with a Black Belt . This number is determined randomly, and changes each day. Complete his request a second time to receive an Expert Belt , and a third time to receive a Focus Sash . After completing all three requests, the cycle repeats.
Pal Park is a special Pokémon preserve in southwest Sinnoh . It allows Trainers to import Pokémon from the distant Kanto and Hoenn regions.

When you first arrive, you find Professor Oak . He introduces you to the park, and explains that Pokémon can be brought here from faraway places, like Kanto and Hoenn . He continues, explaining that the Catching Show held here is a competition to see how quickly these Pokémon can be caught. He's happy to see you visit the park, and thanks you by sharing the Trainer Counter app for the Pokétch. He mentions that he plans to be in Eterna City for a while, where he intends to spend his time studying the Pokémon found in Sinnoh , then exits the building.

With Pal Park now accessible, a new Migrate from <game> option appears on the main menu when the game is loaded, if a Generation III game is loaded into the Nintendo DS 's second slot. This process allows players to transfer Pokémon from one of these games— Ruby, Sapphire , Emerald , FireRed, and LeafGreen Versions —into Diamond and Pearl . Once migrated to a Generation IV game, a Pokémon cannot return to its game of origin.

After selecting the Migrate option, the player is presented with a stripped-down version of the Generation III game's PC on the Nintendo DS ' touch screen. On the upper screen, details about the selected Pokémon are displayed. Pokémon with any move that functions as a field move (referred to as "hidden moves") in the origin game are prohibited. After selecting exactly six Pokémon, the game will prompt the player to confirm that they want to send those Pokémon. Only six Pokémon may be transferred from each Generation III save file in a 24-hour period. After the six Pokémon have been transferred into Generation IV , the Generation III game is no longer required.

When a Catching Show begins, Trainers are tasked with encountering and catching each Pokémon and given 6 Park Balls with which to do so. This special type of Poké Ball never fails, but may only be used during a Catching Show. No other items may be used during a Catching Show.

The park is divided into five biomes, with migrated Pokémon found in the one most like their natural habitat. The two water areas require the use of Surf to encounter any Pokémon. During an encounter, there are only two possible actions: Throw Ball and Run . Should a Trainer decide to run, the Pokémon can still be encountered again until it is caught. Once all six Pokémon have been caught, Trainers may choose to transfer them into their PC Storage System, or keep the Pokémon in the park for a future Catching Show. Trainers do not take ownership of any Pokémon caught here until they transfer them into their PC Storage System. Trainers may leave the park at any time, by leaving through the front entrance or selectin the Retire option from the menu, but the current Catching Show will be cancelled and any Pokémon caught must be recaptured on a subsequent visit.

When you return to Snowpoint City , speak to the Sailor at the pier. He asks if you would like to set sail for the Battle Zone , a large island to the northeast of mainland Sinnoh . The rugged terrain and powerful wild Pokémon provide an excellent opportunity for Trainers to hone their skills. Agree in order to board the S.S. Sinnoh , and the ship departs.

Located between Route 225 to the north and Route 230 to the east, Fight Area is a tiny port town where Trainers who love battling gather to prove their skills. The gateway to the Battle Park is located here.

When the S.S. Sinnoh docks at the pier, you find Barry waiting for you. He wants to be "the greatest Trainer ever", so he is here to toughen up both himself and his Pokémon. A young man nearby overhears Barry, and warns that it will be difficult as Barry is talking about the young man instead. To prove himself, he is heading to the volcano on the north side of the island, which is said to hold a treasure. Barry believes that obtaining this treasure will make him the greatest Trainer and is about to go looking for it, but decides to stop at the Battle Tower first. After he leaves, the young man introduces himself as Buck . He asks if you and Barry know each other, and asks that you tell him not to underestimate the volcano. As he turns to leave, he advises that you both toughen up at the Battle Tower first, as reaching the volcano is no easy feat.
The gate to Battle Park is located on the east side of the Fight Area . The Battle Tower , where the best of the best gather to test their skills, is located here.

When you first enter the gate, you are greeted by the five receptionists and given a Point Card . This card tracks the number of Battle Points won at the Battle Tower until they are redeemed for prizes. These receptionists can then be consulted for more details about challenging the Battle Tower.

The Exchange Service Corner is a large, grand building in the middle of Battle Park . There are two entrances on the ground floor, with an elevated walkway linking the two sides. Inside, Trainers can redeem their hard-earned Battle Points for goods such as TMs and held items .
